evaluation.decision: Compare the fresh R33-supervision and R34-supervision arms and retained PR35 on unchanged frozen 666-front primary and 663-front historical references. Report misses, unmatched outputs, duplicates, empty scenes, zero/one/two-locatable-corner groups and both-corner successes at 5/10 original-image pixels with eligible misses retained in denominators. Report the separately identified current R34 review as exploratory only. Inspect gained/lost identities and the exact training delta. Conflicting reference rankings remain inconclusive; no automatic promotion or new-session reliability claim follows from this run.

limits: The reference arm uses R33 training supervision; the candidate uses eligible R34 supervision. Both are freshly trained together from the original epoch-173 initializer. The comparison isolates the exact hash-bound training-input delta, after the accepted user-named follow-up review in original pixels.

Development amendments do not enter trainer supervision. Original trainer validation remains 664 fronts; frozen 666/663 references are unchanged. The current R34 review is separately identified exploratory evidence only. Training changes are original-pixel boundary/corner corrections, including only the explicitly audited 066:14 visible-left-corner restoration when supported; no hidden point is inferred.

Use L4 or A100. Both fresh arms must have the same recorded runtime. Preserve seed 46, 30 epochs, batch 4, input 1280, FP32, AdamW and final-epoch selection. The unmodified native Pose26 loss is used in both arms. PR113 failed the prespecified clean-improvement screen; partial-box factor2 is discontinued. No threshold/seed/epoch search and no automatic promotion.
hypothesis: Does the exact accepted R34 training-annotation delta improve observed-front localization when both arms use the unchanged native loss and the same fixed seed46 recipe?
prediction_semantics: Hidden-corner estimates remain allowed at inference. A missing annotation is unscorable; it is not proof that a predicted point is physically visible or a false positive.
